questions.stem: Whoever writes the ticket controls `ticket_text`. Which statement about their text is true?

options.text: It reaches line 17 as text that `shell=True` displays but doesn't run
options.why: `shell=True` hands the whole string to the system shell, which runs it as a command.

options.text: It reaches the model, but the model's reply doesn't depend on it
options.why: A model's reply depends on everything in its prompt, and the ticket is in the prompt.
options.origin: misconception: model output is independent of its input

options.text: It can't reach line 17, because `max_tokens=100` limits the reply
options.why: `max_tokens` caps how long the reply is, not what it says. It doesn't cap the prompt either: a long ticket still costs more.

options.text: It can shape the shell command that line 17 runs, via the reply

questions.explain: Follow the value: `ticket_text` goes into `prompt` (line 10), the prompt goes to the model (line 11), the reply becomes `command` (line 16), and line 17 runs it with `shell=True`. Text that reaches a model's prompt can shape its reply (OWASP LLM01), and running a reply unchecked is improper output handling (OWASP LLM05).

path: line 8: `ticket_text` is a parameter the caller controls
line 10: prompt = f"Reply with one shell command that fixes this issue:\n{ticket_text}"

questions.stem: Which change stops the ticket text from writing the command that runs?

options.text: Run only a preset command that the model picks by name
Remove `;`, `&&` and `|` from the reply before running it
options.why: One command can do harm on its own (for example `rm -rf ~`), and a blocklist misses `$( )`, backticks and more. The reply is still the command.
options.origin: misconception; the analyzer still finds the path

options.why: Printing records the command; the next line still runs it.
options.origin: misconception; the analyzer still finds the path

options.text: Add "Never reply with a dangerous command." to the prompt
options.why: An instruction in the prompt is not a security boundary: the ticket text sits in the same prompt and can argue with it (OWASP LLM01, prompt injection).
options.origin: misconception; the analyzer still finds the path

questions.explain: Only in the allowlist version does no path turn ticket text into command text: the command comes from a table of constants, so the ticket can at most pick which preset runs, or none.
